target_customer: Large personal care, home care and food brands that buy palm oil and want a deforestation-free alternative
problem: Palm oil is in a huge share of consumer products and drives deforestation and emissions; no scalable non-agricultural substitute with matching performance existed.
business_model: Ingredient manufacturing and B2B supply and partnerships, with the Palmless consumer line as a showcase brand
product_category: Synthetic biology and precision fermentation ingredients

founders.name: Shara Ticku
education: Harvard Business School (attending at the time per MIT News)
founders.background_notes: MIT News notes experience in fertility health and interest in global health.

founders.name: David Heller
founders.background_notes: Company site lists him as Co-Founder and COO.

founders.name: Harry McNamara
education: PhD candidate, Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as founder; the company site lists only Ticku and Heller.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering yeast to produce palm-like fats and scaling fermentation from milliliters to tens of thousands of liters is research and manufacturing heavy; MIT News says early experiments yielded a few milliliters.

defensibility.rationale: Strain and process know-how, scale-up capacity and food regulatory approvals are hard to copy, though several fermentation rivals emerged.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found as of 2026; large brands showed interest per MIT News and the company stayed independent.

market_need_then: Palm plantation fires caused a 2013 haze crisis in Singapore that motivated the CEO, and consumer brands faced growing pressure over deforestation linked palm oil; no spend numbers at founding were found.

branding.name_origin: Refers to palmitic acid, the 16 carbon fatty acid in palm oil, per search coverage of the founders (the MIT News article did not explain the name).

identity.visual_style: Orange Palmless spray bottle seen in MIT press imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Activist; the earlier product name Torula Oil was modeled on a protest poster as a call to action

branding.brand_signature: The Palmless consumer brand, launched to raise awareness and show large companies the company could partner

rebrands.why: Product naming moved to the Palmless brand; reason and date not stated in opened sources.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch, Fast Company, CNBC and CBS; Palmless trademark filed October 2022 per a trademark listing.

brand_strength.rationale: Palmless is a clear, activist consumer brand that earned press, but the company's growth depends on B2B ingredient deals more than on consumer brand pull.

pivots.from: Earlier first business ideas that did not work
pivots.why: MIT News says the founders started over after their first ideas failed; date approximate.

outcome_analysis: C16 raised a 20 million dollar Series A led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures in March 2020 and added grants and an accelerator investment in January 2024, reaching about 36 million dollars in equity by its own figure. It scaled to metric ton production and is still operating, but profitability and large brand contracts were not verified and several fermentation rivals have appeared.
notes: Total funding conflicts: 24M total after the Series A per 2020 coverage, 36.3M equity plus 2M grants per C16 to TechCrunch in 2024, 34M per Green Queen. About 4M before the Series A (and 12M or more between 2020 and 2024) is not itemized, so no seed or other rounds are recorded. Investor list for Series A comes from search results summarizing 2020 coverage, with Breakthrough Energy Ventures as lead confirmed by the BioLabs page. Founding year 2018 per YC page; some coverage says 2017. No competitor source dated near 2018 found; rivals named in later coverage (Clean Food Group, Xylome, Kiverdi, Genomatica) are undated so excluded. Name origin from search summaries, source page not opened.
